doc.title: Toots Thielemans — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Kenny Clarke and Annie Ross
summary: He recalls Clarke, Annie Ross and the Clarke-Boland Big Band.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: You want to take a break now?
Okay. Oh, you got a minute? You got a few minutes? Go ahead, go ahead.
Yeah. So yeah, you know, when, when people move to, from America to Europe, they forget them here.
I met Kenny Clarke. He was also married to Annie Ross at one time.
Yes. They… Well, I don’t know if they were married, but he did… they have a child. Yeah, Toby, yeah.

And I had met Annie Ross on the seashore, the seashore in Belgium with her aunt [inaudible] or something. And I’m sitting on the beach. And then, later on, because Kenny had this band with the French… the Belgian Francy Boland.

It was a great arrangement and the Boland-Clarke Big Band. And one day, at those times, in those times, I did a lot of guest recordings. You know, you play a few numbers for the radio stations. And I was in Cologne. And that’s where I spent some time with Kenny talking [inaudible]. He said, “You should come to Paris. I hope. That would be nice if you came.” So he was already settled in Paris, yes.
